'''Eric Shannon Moulds''' (born July 17, 1973) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] for 12 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for [[Mississippi State Bulldogs football|Mississippi State University]] and was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] 24th overall in the [[1996 NFL draft]]. In 2009, Moulds (affectionately called E-Money for short) was one of three receivers named to the Buffalo Bills 50th Anniversary All-Time Team.<ref>[http://www.history.buffalobills.com/All-Time+Team Buffalo Bills All-Time Team] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130719213916/http://www.history.buffalobills.com/All-Time+Team |date=July 19, 2013 }}</ref>

'''Eric Henry Laakso''' (November 29, 1956{{spaced ndash}}December 25, 2010) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] and [[Guard (American football)|guard]]. He played seven seasons for the [[Miami Dolphins]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL), a tenure which included two [[Super Bowl]]s.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.norwichbulletin.com/story/sports/high-school/2010/12/28/local-sports-killingly-graduate-ex/44951181007/ |title=Local Sports: Killingly graduate, ex-NFL player dies at 54 |last=Allard |first=Marc |date=27 December 2010 |website=The Bulletin |publisher=Norwich Bulletin |access-date=7 February 2024 |quote=}}</ref> After high school at [[Killingly]] in [[Danielson, Connecticut|Danielson, CT]] he attended [[Tulane University]], where he majored in [[civil engineering]] and played offensive tackle from 1975 to 1977 and was honored as the 1976–77 Tulane Athlete of the year. Laakso was selected 106th overall by the Dolphins in the fourth round of the [[1978 NFL draft]]. Laakso resided in [[South Florida metropolitan area|South Florida]] and was active with [[National Football League Alumni|NFL Alumni]] functions.

Laakso was found dead in his home in Pompano Beach on Christmas night. The death was attributed to natural causes; Laakso battled heart disease.<ref>{{cite news |last=Munzenrider |first=Kyle |date=28 Dec 2010 |title=Former Dolphins Starter Eric Laakso Died on Christmas at Age 53 |url=https://www.miaminewtimes.com/news/former-dolphins-starter-eric-laakso-died-on-christmas-at-age-53-6556408 |work=Miami New Times |location=Sports |access-date=6 Feb 2024}}</ref>

'''Eric Patrick Moore''' (born January 28, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[New York Giants]] ([[1988 NFL season|1988]]–[[1993 NFL season|1993]]), the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] ([[1994 NFL season|1994]]), the [[Cleveland Browns]] ([[1995 Cleveland Browns season|1995]]) and the [[Miami Dolphins]] ([[1995 NFL season|1995]]).  Moore was selected in the first round (tenth overall) of the [[1988 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1988 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1988/draft.htm |access-date=2023-09-23 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  He was a starter for the Giants in their [[Super Bowl XXV]] triumph.

In 1993, Moore was sentenced to a six-month pretrial diversion program for [[steroid]] possession along with former [[New York Giants]] teammate [[Mark Duckens]]. They were described by federal agents as "pawns in international steroid ring."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-01-14-sp-1549-story.html|title=Federal Steroid Case Cites 2 NFL Players|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=January 14, 1993|access-date=2013-09-16}}</ref> Moore was also suspended for the first four weeks of the [[1993 NFL season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1993-07-31-sp-18789-story.html|title=Giants' Moore Gets Month Suspension|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=July 31, 1993|access-date=2013-09-16}}</ref>

Moore lived in the Wolf Creek subdivision in [[Macon, Georgia]] for a while and his nickname in college was "PK".<ref>Mike Freeman, [https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?sec=health&res=9F0CE4DB1739F932A05754C0A965958260 N.F.L. Suspends Moore for Four Games], July 31, 1993</ref>

The murder was committed in league with Nanette Johnston, McLaughlin's live-in girlfriend and Naposki's lover, so that she could collect McLaughlin's life insurance. In July 2011, Naposki was convicted of first degree murder and in August 2012, he was sentenced to life imprisonment without parole.
